answer: A new agent starts in the shadows: it may work, but its rewards stay time-locked and vest only gradually as it builds a clean history. Like a lantern warming up, its trust brightens slowly, so a flood of fresh fake identities earns almost nothing before the round ends. The kernel of the defense is time itself - an attacker cannot echo one identity into a hundred overnight, because each must age through the same slow ramp, and the cost of waiting outruns any gain from the fakes.
